items.why: Tesla reported better-than-expected Q3 deliveries of 486,532 vehicles, ahead of Wall Street's 450,000-460,000 range. Investors read it as continued strength; Baird kept a Buy rating.
AMD climbed with a broad chip-sector advance after soft September payroll data eased pressure on rate expectations. The stock now sits near its 52-week high.
Nvidia led the Nasdaq to an intraday record Friday as chip stocks rallied on the soft jobs data. AI infrastructure demand keeps pulling the complex higher.
The fear gauge sank as Friday's rally took anxiety out of the tape. Soft jobs data revived rate-cut hopes, pulling volatility lower alongside bond yields.

market_note: Futures point higher into Monday's open: ES up 0.7% and NQ up 1.0%.
summary: Friday's softer-than-expected jobs report revived rate-cut hopes and sparked a broad stock rebound. Chip stocks led, with Nvidia pacing the Nasdaq to an intraday record while Tesla surged on strong Q3 deliveries.
